name: Depósito elevado de Chamberí

position.source: https://www.openstreetmap.org/way/48238313 (centroid of the outline of the tower, building=water_tower; the orientation of its twelve sides from the PNOA orthophoto)

rights.note: Elevated water tank of the Canal de Isabel II, idea of Diego Martín Montalvo (1900), designed by the engineer Luis Moya Idígoras (date of death not known) with the pumping plant by Ramón de Aguinaga; built 1907–1911, in service 1912–1952. Converted into an exhibition hall (Sala Canal de Isabel II) in 1986 by the architects Antonio Lopera and Javier Alau. A 20th-century work: taken as protected.

notes: Built by code (model_sources/Q5803317_deposito_elevado_de_chamberi.py, tools/meshkit.py) with AI assistance. The twelve-sided battered brick shaft with a pier on every corner, the recessed window bays (pale panels, brick mullions, bowed transoms and hoods), the gallery of slit openings with brick crosses under a corbelled cornice, the zinc-clad tank (radius 9.25 m) with two round windows a side, its cornice, the ribbed dome with the ventilation ring and the finial; round the foot the plinth on a granite socle with slate lean-to roofs, twelve small pavilions with tiled gables and the arched door. Heights from the 1911 section scaled by the OSM outline (±5 %): the tank roof at about 35 m, the finial to 38 m. Uncertain: which side has the door (taken facing the square, 191°), the exact orientation of the twelve sides (±5°, from the orthophoto), the profile of the dome (photos), the depth of the bays. The garden round it is not part of the OSM element and is not modelled.
